1.2 MAGNE dApp（規劃中）
Dapp Hub：Shin Getter Nexus 是即將推出的整合平台，旨在成為 M Hash 生態系統內去中心化應用程式的統一入口。開發者與使用者可透過一致介面，順暢存取各類 dApp、工具及服務。透過優化 Layer 1 與 Layer 2 的連接，Shin Getter Nexus 致力提升跨應用互通性、降低加入門檻，並促進去中心化經濟發展。
應用 / 規劃中Shin Getter Nexus使用者與開發者DApp Hub擬議的統一入口應用工具服務規劃中的產品概念。此圖為資訊關係圖，並非已發布應用的畫面。

1.1 甚麼是 MAGNE.AI？
MAGNE.AI 是結合 AI 運算基礎設施、DePin 網絡與 Web3 應用的新一代區塊鏈平台。我們致力建立以行動裝置為原生環境、嵌入式且自主運作的 AI 驅動 Web3 世界。
01 / 生態系統從裝置到網絡裝置MAGNE.AI Phone端側 AI · 使用者操作↔應用與開發者工具L1MAGNE基礎網絡L2M Hash應用執行MHA代幣分配與釋放規則詳見代幣經濟章節。概念閱讀圖：呈現白皮書中的設計角色與關係，不代表已驗證的部署狀態。
本項目由兩項基礎技術支撐：

MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈：以行動裝置為優先、相容 EVM 並採用 PoW 的 Layer1 鏈，讓智能手機與邊緣裝置參與挖礦及共識，以保障安全性、去中心化與效能。

MAGNE L1基礎網絡 · EVM 相容性

M Hash Layer2 區塊鏈：基於 opStack 建立的高效能 Layer 2 網絡，採用非同步共識機制，將共識與執行分離，在維持安全性及低交易成本的同時，大幅提高吞吐量與效率。

M Hash L2應用執行 · OP Stack 設計

MAGNE Kit 模組化執行框架：重新設計的執行層，針對低延遲智能合約處理優化，適用於行動場景與 AI 原生工作負載。

MAGNE.AI 引入融合 AI 運算與 Web3 基礎設施的新架構：

使用者分享 MAGNE.AI Phone Gen1 等裝置的閒置算力，即可獲得 $MHA 代幣。
建立由邊緣裝置充當節點的 DePin（去中心化實體基礎設施）網絡。
提供 AI API 與 SDK，讓開發者建立整合 AI 的去中心化應用。
支援 AI 模型在鏈上部署、驗證、定價及使用，實現 Web3 原生 AI 即服務。

MAGNE.AI 生態系統包括：

基礎設施：MAGNE Layer1、M Hash Layer2
裝置矩陣：AI 手機、耳機及眼鏡（規劃中）
應用層：Dapp Hub（Shin Getter Nexus）、AI 助理、Web3 遊戲及 NFT 平台
統一代幣經濟：$MHA 用於 Gas、治理、激勵、質押及存取權限

MAGNE.AI 重新界定「智能裝置」與「去中心化基礎設施」的邊界，支援可信 AI 執行、模型來源追溯、資料所有權及多裝置協作。透過協議與硬件的緊密整合，MAGNE.AI 讓每位使用者都能成為 AI Web3 時代的貢獻者與受益者。

1.3 Magic Hash (MHA)
Magic Hash（簡稱 MHA）目前以 BNB Smart Chain（BSC）上的代幣形式發行與流轉。本白皮書披露的 BSC 合約地址，對應 MHA 現階段的代幣形態。項目計劃在 MAGNE L1 主網與 M Hash L2 網絡具備相應條件後，推進 MHA 向自有網絡體系的遷移與整合。遷移方式、適用網絡、時間安排及持有人需要採取的操作，將另行公告。網絡階段說明下文有關 Gas、區塊獎勵及減半的說明，屬 MAGNE 自有網絡的規劃設計，不代表這些機制已在現階段的 BSC 代幣合約上實現。
MHA分配總量10,000,000,000 MHA分配總量，不代表流通供應量。
交易費用
所有鏈上操作（轉帳、合約呼叫、DApp 互動）均以 $MHA 支付 Gas。按照協議設計，部分費用會被銷毀（與 EVM 費用機制一致），逐步減少流通供應量，形成支持長期價值的通縮壓力。
挖礦與安全
區塊透過 PoW 產生：礦工投入算力打包交易，並競爭下一個區塊的提議權。成功礦工獲得區塊獎勵（$MHA）及交易費用。總算力越高，攻擊成本越高，網絡安全性亦越強。
MAGNE 針對行動及邊緣環境進行優化，讓輕量節點與裝置協助挖礦或中繼，提升去中心化程度及網絡覆蓋。
發行與減半
$MHA 按照先通脹、後減半的規劃發行：初期提供較充足獎勵，其後定期減少，以平衡網絡啟動與長期稀缺性。區塊獎勵與費用銷毀機制共同決定代幣供給與消耗的動態。

1.4 甚麼是工作量證明？
MAGNE Layer 1 的 PoW 工作量證明機制
工作量證明（PoW）是 MAGNE Layer1 網絡的基礎共識機制，透過運算競爭確保去中心化信任、安全交易驗證及網絡抗審查能力。每個節點須解答密碼學難題，以取得區塊提議權，毋須依賴可信中介。MAGNE.AI 將 PoW 重新構想為超越傳統高耗能挖礦的模式，透過整合 DePin（去中心化實體基礎設施），讓智能手機等邊緣裝置成為挖礦節點。此模式讓任何人都能參與共識，並使網絡發展與實際使用相配合。MAGNE PoW 的最終願景，是為 Web3 建立毋須信任、以行動裝置為優先且高度安全的 Layer1 基礎設施。
有別於依賴專用硬件與高能耗的傳統挖礦，MAGNE Layer1 引入輕量 PoW：行動挖礦。配備安全 SPU 與 NPU 晶片的 MAGNE.AI 裝置，讓一般使用者貢獻閒置運算資源、驗證交易並獲取獎勵，形成具包容性的共識層。此模式由 MAGNE 自有 DePin 基礎設施支撐，每台實體裝置均成為區塊鏈節點，不僅是使用者，也是網絡安全驗證者。這種參與式設計降低 Web3 門檻，並促進更公平的價值分配。MAGNE 透過結合 PoW 與邊緣硬件，重新定義去中心化未來的共識模式。
在 MAGNE Layer1 中，PoW 不僅是共識基石，也是效能加速器。項目透過簡化 Merkle Tree 結構及整合智能快取，深度改進 EVM 架構，以最少磁碟 I/O 存取狀態資料，提升執行速度。智能合約因而獲得更低延遲及更高吞吐量，適合高頻應用。此基礎設計亦配合未來 Layer2 擴展，確保模組化鏈之間順暢同步資料。在 MAGNE 中，PoW 既是防護盾，也是引擎，同時保障鏈的安全並提升能力。
受 Berachain 流動性證明（Proof of Liquidity，PoL）等架構啟發，MAGNE 將共識與治理解耦。PoW 專注保障網絡安全，決策與投票則透過鏈上 MHA 代幣進行。此職責分離讓 Layer1 專注效能及安全，同時將治理權交予更廣泛的社群，避免礦工主導協議控制所帶來的中心化風險。

Eᵢ,ₘ = Pₘ × (0.20 × Aᵢ,ₘ + 0.80 × Wᵢ,ₘ)

月內新增或退出設備時，以資格變動時間切分互不重疊的子期間 j；各段時長比例 dⱼ = Δtⱼ / Tₘ，全月合計為 1。每段僅使用 Bₘ × dⱼ 的預算，Nⱼ 為該段合資格且去重的設備數。該設備未准入的段落獎勵為零；Nⱼ = 0 時該段新增獎勵為零。Eᵢ,ₘ = Σⱼ [dⱼ × min(Bₘ / max(Nⱼ, 13,750), 10,000) × (0.20 × Aᵢ,ⱼ + 0.80 × Wᵢ,ⱼ)]Aᵢ,ⱼ 與 Wᵢ,ⱼ 分別以該段完整時長及對應參考任務能力為分母，仍須滿足 0 ≤ Wᵢ,ⱼ ≤ Aᵢ,ⱼ ≤ 1。不得將全月比例再次套入分段公式而重複折算。參考能力換算、超標任務量的核驗／封頂方式及結算時區須在啟用前公布。基礎測算器僅支援每月設備數固定的情境，不計算月內分段；設備及已核定批次各自記帳，不以當前設備數重算歷史獎勵。

Uᵢ,ₘ = 0.60 × Eᵢ,ₘ + 0.20 × Eᵢ,ₘ₋₁ + 0.20 × Eᵢ,ₘ₋₂

1.6 治理
MAGNE.AI 的治理系統讓 $MHA 持有人直接參與協議層決策，投票權與持幣數量成正比。治理如同網絡的大腦：核心協議行為的任何變更，均須通過鏈上治理流程，確保透明度及去中心化控制。
治理職責
治理機構負責協議運作與長期方向的策略決策，包括：

設定費用、質押獎勵及協議參數
批准協議升級與核心模組更換
管理特權角色與存取權限
制定長期增長、激勵及生態發展方向

所有重大變更均須在執行前，完成正式治理提案與投票週期。
協議角色與權限
管理者角色（Manager）
管理者負責處理需要即時執行的緊急協議操作，例如在出現威脅時暫停資金池或金庫。管理者亦須執行已經治理批准的營運變更，讓系統在預先界定的治理範圍內迅速行動。
授權者角色（Authorizer）
授權者是協議的權限控制者，連接治理決策與可執行的協議功能。透過對每項敏感操作實施授權邏輯，確保整個系統的存取控制安全。授權者與治理時間鎖協作，確保所有變更經審核後安全執行。
協調者角色（Coordinator）
協調者監督治理提案的最終執行階段，管理升級的分階段部署、先後次序及時機，確保所有操作符合協議規則。若部署期間出現問題，協調者亦有緊急權力取消或延遲變更，以維護治理流程完整性。

1.7 治理概覽
1.7.1 MAGNE 治理
MAGNE 的去中心化治理系統，讓 $MHA 代幣持有人主導協議層變更，包括獎勵金庫批准、原生 dApp 設定及 PoW 分配邏輯。
治理應用場景：

將獎勵金庫加入白名單（例如批准質押／激勵代幣）
設定 MAGNESwap 等原生 dApp（例如費用結構）
調整流動性證明（Proof of Liquidity，PoL）的分配曲線或參數
升級系統設定或時間鎖期限


治理生命週期
MAGNE 治理建基於經實務驗證的 OpenZeppelin 合約，提供安全透明的多階段生命週期：


建立提案
任何具備足夠投票權的帳戶均可發起提案


待啟動狀態
提案先經過 1 小時短暫延遲，然後啟動投票


投票階段
$MHA 持有人或其受託代表可在 5 天投票期內投票


提案結果
若達到法定參與門檻及多數票要求，提案標記為通過


時間鎖佇列
通過的提案須進入 2 天延遲佇列，然後執行


執行
時間鎖到期後，任何參與者均可在鏈上執行變更



守護者監督
為防止惡意行為，MAGNE 採用 5-of-9 守護者委員會，有權在時間鎖階段取消危險提案，例如未經授權的升級或資產沒收。

建立治理提案


確認符合投票權門檻
您須具備至少相當於 10,000 $MHA 的委託投票權


委託予自己
您須明確委託 $MHA（即使受託人是自己），才可啟用治理權


準備提案資料
例如，獎勵金庫提案須包含金庫地址及正確函式呼叫，例如 addRewardVault(address)


提交提案
透過鏈上治理合約或 MAGNEHub 介面提交


推廣提案
與社群交流，提升認知並爭取投票支持


時間鎖到期後執行
提案通過後，任何使用者均可在 2 天延遲期結束後觸發執行



治理參數（預設值）
狀態條件建立提案10,000 $MHA 委託票數待啟動期1 小時投票期5 天法定參與門檻$MHA 總供應量的 20%時間鎖延遲2 天

獎勵金庫提案可採用簡化治理流程，詳見獎勵金庫治理文件。

1.8 激勵市場
在 M Hash Layer2 PoW 生態中，激勵市場讓協議向礦工提供白名單激勵代幣，鼓勵其支援特定鏈上活動或流動性池。不同協議因此競爭礦工關注與區塊獎勵配置。
激勵運作方式
礦工產生區塊時，可選擇將部分所得 $MHA 獎勵分配至一個或多個白名單獎勵金庫。這些金庫與特定協議或應用相連。
分配獎勵時：

礦工獲得協議以激勵代幣支付的佣金
金庫其餘激勵代幣分配予已在該金庫質押合資格資產的參與者
所有領取均透過 M Hash Layer2 Hub 自動處理
使用者可隨時領取激勵，沒有到期限制

激勵市場角色
角色說明參與者將合資格資產（例如 LP 代幣、NFT）質押至獎勵金庫，以獲取激勵礦工透過 PoW 產生區塊，將部分 $MHA 獎勵導向選定金庫，以換取激勵協議提供激勵代幣，吸引礦工導入獎勵，提升參與度及流動性
激勵代幣治理

只有白名單獎勵金庫可分配激勵代幣
每個金庫最多支援兩種不同激勵代幣
新增代幣或變更其管理者須經治理批准

管理激勵
協議的代幣管理者須設定激勵兌換率：

格式：「每 MHA 對應 X 枚代幣」（例如 10 USDC/MHA）
除非金庫代幣餘額已完全耗盡，否則不得調低兌換率
可隨時存入額外代幣，亦可提高兌換率
激勵代幣一旦存入，便不得提取

範例：
激勵兌換率$MHA 覆蓋量2000 USDC10/$MHA200 $MHA
其後更新：
新增激勵新兌換率新覆蓋量2500 USDC11/$MHA227 $MHA
佣金分配

礦工可設定從金庫取得激勵的佣金比例（預設 5%，最高 20%）
範例：若金庫為 10 MHA 支付 100 USDC，而佣金比例為 5% 的礦工導入價值 1 MHA 的獎勵，礦工獲得 5 USDC，其餘 95 USDC 分配予金庫參與者。

時間安排與兌換率

分配時間（例如 3 天或 7 天串流釋放）由獎勵金庫設定
無論獎勵釋放時間如何安排，兌換率（例如 10 USDC/$MHA）均保持固定

1.9 團隊與執行
團隊與執行
MAGNE.AI 由跨領域團隊開發，涵蓋安全行動系統、Web3 基礎設施（L1／L2）、安全工程、硬件項目執行及全球生態營運。
安全與私隱工程
專注安全架構設計、經認證安全元件整合、漏洞研究及持續安全保障。此職能負責威脅建模、全技術堆疊安全審查及事故應變準備。
區塊鏈與協議工程（L1／L2）
負責協議開發、節點基礎設施、效能與穩定性優化，以及支援生態合作夥伴的開發工具。
行動裝置與錢包產品工程
建立面向消費者的作業系統／應用層、錢包及帳戶流程，以及簡化操作複雜度的使用者體驗，同時維持自主託管及安全性。
硬件項目與合規執行
領導端到端裝置項目，包括平台選型、供應商整合、驗證及產能爬坡階段（EVT／DVT／PVT），以及各地區認證準備。
業務拓展與生態營運
推動合作夥伴加入、交易所與機構協調，以及兼顧合規的營運；支援合作夥伴盡職調查及合規流程（例如適用的 KYC／AML 工作流程），並促進全球社群發展。
擴展貢獻者與合作夥伴
除核心團隊外，MAGNE.AI 亦獲製造、元件供應、認證服務及生態發展領域的貢獻者與策略合作夥伴支援，以加快交付並確保量產品質。
治理與交付紀律
MAGNE.AI 在產品、工程、安全與營運之間維持清晰職責分工，並以標準化開發流程及受控發布管理作支援。對外溝通遵循披露政策，旨在確保準確性，避免前瞻性上市或價格相關陳述。詳細團隊及認證資料，可透過受控盡職調查流程提供予交易所、合作夥伴及監管機構。
註：基於私隱及安全考量，部分履歷及資歷可能以摘要形式呈現。詳細資料可在保密協議／受控審查下提供。

1.10 MAGNE Layer2 指標
與建立在 PoW 或相容以太坊 Layer 1 鏈上的其他 Layer 2 擴容方案相比，M Hash Layer2 提供更低 Gas 費及更高區塊 Gas 上限，讓費用在 Layer 2 流量增加時仍保持穩定。下表以標準 EIP-1559 參數作比較；部分 L2（例如 Arbitrum）採用 ArbOS 等自訂 Gas 機制，不能直接比較。

4.3 建立智能合約
4.3.1 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈
4.3.2 部署智能合約

協助您開始在 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈部署智能合約的指南。

歡迎使用 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈部署快速入門指南！本指南將逐步協助您設定環境，並在 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈部署智能合約。無論您是資深開發者或剛入門，都可依照本指南操作。
4.3.3 您將完成甚麼
完成本快速入門後，您將能夠：

設定用於 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈部署的開發環境
將智能合約部署至 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈
將前端連接至智能合約
為何選擇 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈？

MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈以行動裝置為優先，相容 EVM 並採用 PoW，讓智能手機與邊緣裝置參與挖礦及共識，以保障安全性、去中心化與效能。
4.3.4 設定開發環境

建立新的項目目錄

複製mkdir my-MAGNE-project && cd my-MAGNE-project


安裝功能強大的智能合約開發框架 Foundry

複製curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup

此操作會安裝 Foundry，並更新至最新版本。

初始化新的 Solidity 項目

複製
複製forge init

Foundry 項目已準備就緒。您可在 src 目錄找到範例合約，並將其替換為自己的合約。本指南採用 src/Counter.sol 提供的 Counter 合約。
Foundry 提供一組 EVM 應用開發工具，包括 Forge（測試）、Cast（與鏈互動）及 Anvil（建立本地節點）。您可在此處進一步了解 Foundry。
4.3.5 設定 Foundry 連接 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈
要將智能合約部署至 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈，您需要兩項關鍵要素：

用於與 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈網絡互動的節點連接
具有足夠資金、可用於部署合約的私鑰

以下逐一設定：
1. 設定節點連接

在項目根目錄建立 .env 檔案
將 MagicalHash 網絡 RPC URL 加入 .env 檔案

複製MAGICAL_RPC_URL="https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com"


載入環境變數

複製source .env

Magne L1 Testnet 是 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈的測試網，本指南其餘部分均使用該網絡。您可透過水龍頭免費取得測試用 MHA。
2. 安全保存私鑰

將私鑰儲存於 Foundry 安全金鑰庫

複製cast wallet import deployer --interactive


依提示輸入私鑰及密碼。

私鑰儲存於 ~/.foundry/keystores，此位置不受 Git 追蹤。
切勿分享私鑰或將其提交至版本控制。務必安全保存並謹慎處理。
4.3.6 部署合約
環境設定完成後，即可將合約部署至 Magne L1 Testnet。

使用以下指令編譯並部署合約

複製forge create ./src/Counter.sol:Counter --rpc-url $MAGICAL_RPC_URL --account deployer

請注意，部署合約的格式為 <contract-path>:<contract-name>。

部署成功後，主控台會輸出交易雜湊
複製已部署合約地址，並加入 .env 檔案

複製COUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x..."


載入新的環境變數

複製source .env

驗證部署
確認合約已成功部署：

在 https://explorer.testnet.magicalhash.com 查閱交易。
使用 cast 指令，從命令列與已部署合約互動

複製cast call $COUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS "number()(uint256)" --rpc-url $MAGNE_RPC_URL

此操作會傳回 Counter 合約 number 儲存變數的初始值，即 0。
恭喜！您已將智能合約部署至 MAGNE L1 鏈！

具有足夠資金、可用於部署合約的私鑰

以下逐一設定：
1. 設定節點連接

在項目根目錄建立 .env 檔案
將 M Hash Layer2 區塊鏈網絡 RPC URL 加入 .env 檔案

複製MAGICAL_RPC_URL="https://l2-rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com"


載入環境變數

複製source .env

M Hash L2 Testnet 是 M Hash Layer2 區塊鏈的測試網，本指南其餘部分均使用該網絡。您可透過水龍頭免費取得測試用 MHA。
2. 安全保存私鑰

將私鑰儲存於 Foundry 安全金鑰庫

複製cast wallet import deployer --interactive


依提示輸入私鑰及密碼。

私鑰儲存於 ~/.foundry/keystores，此位置不受 Git 追蹤。
切勿分享私鑰或將其提交至版本控制。務必安全保存並謹慎處理。
4.3.12 部署合約
環境設定完成後，即可將合約部署至 M Hash L2 Testnet。

使用以下指令編譯並部署合約

複製forge create ./src/Counter.sol:Counter --rpc-url $MAGICAL_RPC_URL --account deployer

請注意，部署合約的格式為 <contract-path>:<contract-name>。

部署成功後，主控台會輸出交易雜湊
複製已部署合約地址，並加入 .env 檔案

複製COUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x..."


載入新的環境變數

複製source .env

驗證部署
確認合約已成功部署：

在 https://l2-explorer.testnet.magicalhash.com 查閱交易。
使用 cast 指令，從命令列與已部署合約互動

複製cast call $COUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS "number()(uint256)" --rpc-url $MAGNE_RPC_URL

此操作會傳回 Counter 合約 number 儲存變數的初始值，即 0。
恭喜！您已將智能合約部署至 M Hash L2 鏈！

all.text:
4.4 使用 Foundry 發行 ERC-20 代幣

4.4.1 0）先決條件


Foundry v1.3.1+
複製curl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup

（Etherscan V2 驗證需要 Foundry v1.3.1 或更新版本。）



4.4.2 1）建立項目
複製mkdir launch-mha-token && cd launch-mha-token
forge init

此操作會建立標準 Foundry 項目結構。

4.4.3 2）安裝 OpenZeppelin 並設定路徑映射
複製forge install OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts
echo 'remappings = ["@openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/"]' >> foundry.toml


此設定可確保 IDE 正確解析 OpenZeppelin 匯入路徑。

4.4.4 3）編寫 ERC-20 合約
重新命名預設檔案：
複製mv src/Counter.sol src/MagnetToken.sol

src/MagnetToken.sol:
複製// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import {ERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol";

contract MagnetToken is ERC20 {
    constructor(
        string memory name_,
        string memory symbol_,
        uint256 initialSupply
    ) ERC20(name_, symbol_) {
        _mint(msg.sender, initialSupply);
    }
}

編譯以確認：
複製forge compile


4.4.5 4）建立部署腳本
重新命名範例腳本並更新內容：
複製mv script/Counter.s.sol script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol

script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol:
複製// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import {Script, console2} from "forge-std/Script.sol";
import {MagnetToken} from "../src/MagnetToken.sol";

contract DeployMagnetToken is Script {
    function run() public {
        vm.startBroadcast();
        // Example: 1,000,000 tokens (18 decimals)
        MagnetToken token = new MagnetToken("Magic Hash", "MHA", 1_000_000 ether);
        vm.stopBroadcast();

        console2.log("address:", address(token));
        console2.log("totalSupply:", token.totalSupply());
    }
}



4.4.6 5）（可選）調整測試
複製mv test/Counter.t.sol test/MagnetToken.t.sol

您可留空，或加入自己的代幣測試。

4.4.7 6）建立 Foundry 金鑰庫錢包
複製cast wallet import MyMagneAccount --interactive
# paste private key, set password

此帳戶將用於部署。

4.4.8 7）本地試跑（可選）
複製anvil
# new terminal:
forge script script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol \
  --account MyMagneAccount \
  --fork-url https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com \
  --broadcast


您將看到已部署地址及總供應量的日誌。

4.4.9 8）部署至 MAGNE L1 測試網
確認錢包持有 MAGNE L1 測試網代幣，以支付 Gas。
複製forge script script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol \
  --account MyMagneAccount \
  --rpc-url https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com \
  --broadcast


輸出內容將包括交易雜湊及已部署合約地址。

💡 您可切換至主網 RPC（例如 https://rpc.magicalhash.com），將此流程調整用於主網。


4.4.10 9）在 MAGNE L1 瀏覽器驗證合約
MAGNE.AI 採用相容 Etherscan 的驗證方式。您需要 API 金鑰：
複製forge verify-contract \
  --watch \
  --chain magne-ai-testnet \
  <0xYOUR_DEPLOYED_CONTRACT_ADDRESS> \
  src/MagnetToken.sol:MagnetToken \
  --verifier etherscan \
  --etherscan-api-key <YOUR_API_KEY>


驗證完成後，可在 MAGNE L1 瀏覽器檢視合約頁面。

4.4.11 10）快速檢查清單

✅ 代幣名稱／符號（"Magic Hash"、"MHA"）
✅ 初始供應量使用 ether（18 位小數）
✅ RPC：https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com/
✅ 錢包：MyMagneAccount
✅ 驗證用 API 金鑰
✅ 用於 Gas 的測試網 MAGNE 餘額

3.2 為何 M Hash Layer2 建基於 OP Stack
在建立 M Hash Layer2 前，團隊對可用的 Layer 2 框架進行了廣泛研究與評估。最終選擇 OP Stack 作為 M Hash Layer2 Rollup 基礎，原因在於其模組化、高效能潛力，以及與我們目標的一致性。
3.2.1 我們的目標

達到最高每秒 100M Gas 吞吐量。我們優化 EVM 執行、狀態儲存及交易處理，推進 Layer 2 效能上限。
提供極低成本的 Rollup 方案。由於 Layer 1 calldata 成本佔 Rollup 費用主要部分，我們設計 M Hash Layer2 支援靈活的資料可用性（DA）層，毋須僅依賴主網發布，從而大幅降低 Gas 開支。
貢獻開放基礎設施。M Hash Layer2 的所有效能優化及研究將開源，並與更廣泛的 OP Stack 生態共享。

3.2.2 為何選擇 OP Stack

模組化執行客戶端：OP Stack 讓 M Hash Layer2 插入不同執行客戶端，以調校效能或提升去中心化。我們可整合現有相容 BSC 的客戶端，或建立自有執行層。
靈活資料可用性：OP Stack 將執行層與 DA 層分離。M Hash Layer2 可在 Ethereum DA、BNB Greenfield 或未來自訂 DA 層之間選擇，以平衡安全性、擴展能力及成本。
生態互通性：作為 OP Stack 生態一員，M Hash Layer2 可連接 Optimism 等其他 Rollup，提升網絡效應、可組合性及生態間合作。

3.3 為何 MAGNE.AI 需要 Layer2
Layer 1（L1）是負責資料傳播及共識的基礎結算與安全層；在我們的生態中，這就是 MAGNE（PoW，原生代幣 $MHA）。當熱門應用（GameFi、SocialFi、迷因幣發行、NFT 鑄造等）短時間內帶來大量互動，L1 在高峰期容易擁塞：Gas 費急升、確認變慢、使用者體驗下降，同鏈其他 dApp 亦可能受影響。
為解決此問題，L1 需要擴展能力，即在不犧牲安全性的前提下，每秒處理更多交易。實務上，單純擴大單鏈往往會犧牲去中心化程度或安全邊界。較可行的路徑是引入 Layer 2（L2）；我們採用的 M Hash Layer2 基於 opStack，利用非同步批次共識提供低成本與高吞吐量。
3.3.1 L1 在高峰負載下的挑戰

交易擁塞：當每日交易激增至數百萬筆，L1 區塊空間變得稀缺，排隊及打包延遲明顯。
費用急升：Gas 競價推高互動成本，使新使用者與長尾場景難以負擔，阻礙應用增長。
效能外溢影響：單一高流量 dApp 的流量高峰，可拖慢鏈上所有其他應用的確認與最終確定時間。


例如，若 Web3 遊戲在高峰期每天產生 8,000,000+ 筆交易，僅在 L1 處理不但造成確認延遲及同步壓力，亦可能令每日 Gas 成本難以持續，抑制真實使用者增長與留存。

3.3.2 M Hash Layer2（L2）如何提供協助

分擔運算與資料：先在 L2 執行及聚合交易批次，再將摘要發布至 L1；L1 專注安全及最終結算，L2 處理高頻低成本執行。
高吞吐量、低費用：透過 opStack 的執行／共識分離與非同步批次處理，大幅提升吞吐量並降低單筆交易邊際成本，適合交易、遊戲、社交及支付等高頻場景。
可組合且相容：相容 EVM，開發者與使用者可沿用熟悉的工具鏈及錢包；資產與狀態可在 L1、L2 間順暢橋接。
維持安全性：資料與最終確定性錨定於 L1（MAGNE／PoW／$MHA），在擴展時維持去中心化與安全邊界。

3.3.3 對 $MHA 與生態的正面影響

減輕費用壓力：將大部分高頻互動遷移至 L2，降低 L1 的 $MHA Gas 壓力，避免高峰期區塊空間競價戰。
更強網絡效應：低成本與高效能吸引更多真實使用者及開發者，進而增加 L1 結算與安全需求，推動算力及經濟安全增長。
可持續增長：熱門 dApp 可擴展，而不排擠整條鏈的使用體驗，讓生態並行發展，避免「增長等於擁塞」的困局。

結論：
MAGNE（L1／PoW／$MHA）提供安全性與最終確定性，M Hash Layer2（L2）提供高吞吐量及低費用。兩者共同確保生態在極端應用負載下仍可用、可負擔且可持續，毋須犧牲去中心化或安全性。

3.5 高安全性應用
高安全性應用
MAGNE Layer1 透過工作量證明共識及鏈上透明審計提供穩健安全保障。
所有交易、合約執行及資金流向，均可在區塊鏈公開驗證且不可竄改。
因此適合需要最高安全標準的應用，例如金融服務、去中心化治理、供應鏈資料驗證及合規審計。
使用者與機構毋須依賴第三方，即可獨立驗證系統完整性，降低信任成本並提升整體可信度。

3.6 M Hash Layer2 在 OP Stack 上的優化
為提升 M Hash Layer2 Rollup 吞吐量並降低 Gas 費，我們在 OP Stack 的執行層及推導層引入多項效能優化。這些改進建基於針對高吞吐量 Layer 2 網絡的研究及工程工作。
執行層優化
EVM 狀態存取優化
M Hash Layer2 透過改進快取層級，優化 EVM 存取狀態的方式。類似 BSC 的 SharedPool 概念，我們引入 Level 1.5（L1.5）快取，提升記憶體與磁碟儲存之間的資料存取效率，降低執行延遲。
提高 Diff Layer 的布隆過濾器準確度
布隆過濾器用於在狀態查找時檢查鍵值對是否存在，但資料量大會增加誤判。M Hash Layer2 將 Diff Layer 深度由 128 減至 32，縮小過濾器資料佔用，減少不必要的遞迴快取查找，顯著提高 EVM 狀態取得效率。
透過共享快取高效預取
預取在區塊執行前，將狀態資料預載至快取以加快交易處理。過往主執行緒與預取執行緒使用獨立快取，限制效能。現採用共享世界狀態池（originStorage），讓兩個執行緒直接存取 L1.5 快取，大幅提高區塊處理的快取命中率。
L2 區塊產生快取
提議區塊時，交易通常執行兩次：產生區塊時一次，提交酬載時再一次。我們引入快取層，儲存首次執行結果。收到最終確認呼叫（engine_newPayloadV1）時，M Hash Layer2 直接從快取取得預先計算的酬載，降低延遲。
推導層優化
非同步批次提交
過往批次提交器須等待 L1 的 15 次確認（約 45s），才提交新批次。為提高吞吐量，我們實作非同步提交：批次毋須等待即可送出，背景監察器則監控 L1 重組；若發生重組，受影響批次會重新提交。此升級大幅提升 L2 吞吐量，並計劃於未來主網版本發布。

3.7 硬件賦能：安全與運算的融合

2.1 Gas 與費用
M Hash Layer2 是建立在 MAGNE Layer 1 區塊鏈之上的擴容方案，旨在為 DeFi、NFT、遊戲及其他高需求應用提供高吞吐量與低成本交易。
M Hash Layer2 的交易成本由兩部分組成：

Layer 2 Gas 費：反映在 M Hash L2 處理交易所需的運算複雜度
Layer 1 Gas 費：支付將交易批次提交至 MAGNE 主網作驗證及最終確認的成本

Gas 價格公式： Gas 價格 = 基本價格 + 優先價格
交易成本公式： L2 交易成本 =（L2 Gas 價格 × L2 Gas 用量）+（L1 Gas 價格 × L1 Gas 用量）

目前設定
網絡基本價格下限最低優先價格M Hash L2 測試網0 gwei1 gweiM Hash L2 主網MAGNE L1 測試網0 gwei0.1 gweiMAGNE L1 主網

含義
基本價格下限是 M Hash 可設定的最低基本 Gas 價格，此值可隨網絡使用情況動態變更。例如按目前設定，若區塊使用量達到 100M Gas 上限的 50%，基本價格將上升 12.5%。
最低優先價格預先設定；使用者可選擇高於此最低值的任意優先費。錢包及 dApp 通常呼叫「估算 Gas 價格」API，按最近區塊的平均 Gas 價格取得建議 Gas 價格。
M Hash 的目標是將基本轉帳成本維持在 $0.001 以下，促進大規模採用，並支援高頻、低金額場景。
M Hash Layer2 如何維持低成本

增強資料壓縮：採用先進壓縮演算法，在提交至 L1 前盡量縮小 L2 交易資料
高效交易批次處理：優化批次，以提高區塊空間使用率並降低單筆交易成本
資料可用性方案：利用 MAGNE 的資料可用性基礎設施，分擔部分 L1 儲存需求，降低成本
零知識證明：毋須暴露完整交易資料即可驗證交易，減少 L1 資料負載
協議層優化：改進協議執行及網絡通訊，降低 L2 運算開支

2.3 MAGNE.AI Layer2 — M Hash
網絡 / 閱讀圖M Hash L201應用請求使用者透過錢包與應用操作。02L2 執行在 L2 設計中處理交易。03L1 互動提交與驗證方式取決於實際部署配置。概念閱讀圖：呈現白皮書中的設計角色與關係，不代表已驗證的部署狀態。
2.3.1 Layer2 架構
MAGNE.AI 的 M Hash Layer2 架構，旨在滿足現代 Web3 應用的高並行、低延遲及即時互動需求。其建基於優化版 opStack 框架，捨棄傳統共識機制，採用重視速度與回應能力的精簡結構。系統僅包含兩個關鍵角色：執行節點（opgas）及狀態同步器（opnode），在維持資料完整性的同時提高效率。
opgas 節點批次執行區塊交易，毋須逐項操作確認。批次完成後，opnode 在一次共識步驟中驗證整組結果。此非同步批次處理設計突破傳統同步執行瓶頸，適合交易平台、區塊鏈遊戲、社交應用及支付方案等高效能應用。
每個鏈上應用均以具有獨立執行邏輯的 Rollup 實作，提供靈活性與隔離性。開發者可透過統一高效能 API 層，順暢存取鏈上及鏈下資料。架構在設計上適合行動裝置，讓使用者直接透過專用應用使用 Web3 功能，毋須依賴瀏覽器或擴充功能。
儘管移除共識協議，M Hash Layer2 仍透過多層驗證、重放保護及故障復原功能，維持強一致性與安全性。結合 opStack 模組化設計，M Hash Layer2 具備高度可自訂性及擴展能力，支援持續演進的 Web3 生態需求。
總括而言，M Hash Layer2 代表高效能區塊鏈基礎設施的新模式。透過簡化共識、平行處理及直觀使用者體驗，為下一代 Web3 創新及輕量鏈架構提供技術基礎。
2.3.2 Layer2 創新
MAGNE.AI 在 M Hash Layer2 設計中引入新的非同步共識機制，將交易執行（opgas）與共識操作（opnode）解耦。此架構大幅提升高效能 Web3 與 AI 整合應用的擴展能力、吞吐量及回應速度。
傳統 Layer2 Rollup 系統中，執行與排序緊密耦合，所有交易須由同一組驗證者或排序器依序處理。此設計雖簡單，但會限制平行處理能力，並在高交易量或鏈上 AI 推論等複雜工作負載下形成瓶頸。
M Hash Layer2 透過兩個核心元件分離這些職責：

opgas（執行層）：獨立處理交易邏輯、合約執行及 AI 模型推論。
opnode（共識層）：負責批次處理、排序，並向 Layer1 提交已驗證結果。

透過非同步運作，多個 opgas 單元可平行處理交易、預先執行並快取結果，同時由 opnode 完成共識及向基礎鏈發布。此結構盡量減少同步延遲，提升執行效率。
此架構的主要優點包括：

更高吞吐量：多條執行通道可處理並行交易及高運算量操作。
更低延遲：本地預確認與執行緩衝讓使用者互動更快。
模組化擴展：opgas 與 opnode 可獨立擴展，並部署於分散式網絡。
具韌性的驗證：非同步設計可在最終提交前，靈活合併結果並解決衝突。

因此，M Hash Layer2 特別適合需要智能合約、即時推論及資料可用性大規模共存的 AI x Web3 場景。非同步共識模式實現真正平行處理，為下一代回應迅速且智能化的去中心化應用鋪路。

2.4 MAGNE.AI Layer1 — MAGNE
網絡 / 閱讀圖MAGNE L101交易錢包或應用提交請求。02執行合約邏輯讀取並更新狀態。03網絡紀錄區塊記錄交易與執行後狀態。概念閱讀圖：呈現白皮書中的設計角色與關係，不代表已驗證的部署狀態。
2.4.1 Layer1 架構
MAGNE.AI 的 MAGNE Layer1 區塊鏈採用工作量證明（PoW）共識機制，優先考量安全性、抗審查能力及完全去中心化。此設計透過無許可運算驗證每筆交易與狀態更新，提供可抵禦女巫攻擊及拜占庭故障的毋須信任基礎。
MAGNE 完全相容以太坊虛擬機（EVM），讓開發者以極低轉換成本部署現有智能合約，並沿用熟悉工具。EVM 相容性不僅加快加入流程，亦為順暢 Layer2 整合與擴展奠定基礎。
作為 MAGNE.AI 生態骨幹，MAGNE 為去中心化 AI 執行及現實世界基礎設施協調提供安全穩定基礎。它不僅是共識層，更是支援全球規模智能應用的信任層。
2.4.2 Layer1 代幣
MHA 代幣是 MAGNE 網絡的核心功能及治理資產，主要用於支付交易與智能合約執行的 Gas 費，同時支援價值累積及去中心化治理。
MHA 採用動態減半模式，發放量按區塊高度及網絡活動自動調整，在提供早期採用激勵的同時維持長期稀缺性，促進可持續價值增長。以 MHA 支付的 Gas 費部分被銷毀或重新分配予驗證者，使代幣用途與實際鏈上使用緊密連結，形成活動越多、價值越高的回饋循環。
除功能用途外，MHA 讓持有人參與鏈上治理，就費用模型、金庫配置及網絡升級等關鍵協議決策提出提案及投票。此機制鞏固去中心化，讓社群共同決定平台未來。
2.4.3 Layer1 創新
MAGNE 引入超越傳統區塊鏈設計的架構創新，回應高吞吐量 AI 應用及去中心化實體基礎設施的特定需求。主要改進包括優化儲存架構及強化安全機制，兩者均對可擴展且安全的去中心化運算至關重要。
優化儲存架構
傳統 EVM 鏈高度依賴 Merkle Tree 驗證狀態完整性。此結構雖安全，但中間節點雜湊計算複雜，會產生顯著效能開支，在高頻智能合約執行或 AI 狀態轉換下尤為明顯。
MAGNE 引入輕量狀態證明模型，在不犧牲可驗證性的前提下，減少對 Merkle 中間節點的依賴。結合分片狀態存取與快取層加速，此方式大幅提高讀寫效率、降低 Gas 成本並增加總吞吐量，尤其適合狀態快速頻繁變更的 AI 環境。
強化安全機制
透過多層驗證進一步強化安全性：除核心 PoW 共識外，加入活躍驗證者子集，負責關鍵合約及互動的執行時驗證。此架構提高對重放、合約重入及未授權資料修改等攻擊的抵抗能力。
平台亦採用鏈上信譽追蹤與分散式金鑰管理，減少中心化單點故障，並提升惡意環境下的信任復原能力。未來版本將整合基於 ZK 的狀態證明，進一步加強完整性檢查，實現信任最小化 AI 執行。
這些創新均經模組化，並透過可程式化介面提供予開發者，讓團隊在預設具有效能與安全性的基礎上開發，同時保留靈活性及去中心化。

5.1 常見問題
5.1.1 MAGNE 常見問題（FAQ）


M Hash L2 的效能指標為何？
M Hash L2 目前提供：



出塊時間：約 2 秒
TPS：每秒數千筆交易，視乎 Gas 用量及區塊大小
最終確定性：單時隙最終確定性，提供快速安全確認。



甚麼是 DEX？
DEX（去中心化交易所）是一種完全透過智能合約進行鏈上代幣兌換的協議，毋須依賴中心化中介。


甚麼是兌換？
兌換是將一種代幣換成另一種代幣的過程，例如將 USDC 換成 MHA，即表示賣出 USDC 並買入 MHA。


兌換需要多少費用？
兌換費率視乎資金池而異，一般為 0.05%、0.1%、0.3% 或 1%。執行兌換前應先確認費率。


甚麼是流動性？
流動性指可供兌換的代幣數量。流動性越高，滑價越低，價格越佳。


甚麼是流動性池？
流動性池由使用者存入兩種或以上代幣組成，讓 DEX 能夠進行代幣兌換。


甚麼是流動性提供者？
流動性提供者（LP）是向流動性池存入代幣的使用者，可分享該池產生的交易費用。


甚麼是 APY？
APY 指年化收益率，即提供流動性的年度回報率，主要來自兌換費用。


甚麼是 $MHA？
$MHA 是 MAGNE 網絡唯一的原生代幣，用於 Gas、質押、治理及激勵。



總供應量固定。
總供應量的 15%分配予驗證者及質押獎勵。
發放遵循減半時間表:


第 1 年：釋放 7.5%


第 2 年：釋放 3.75%


第 3 年：釋放 1.875%


依此類推。
此安排確保長期可持續性，並控制代幣通脹。






MAGNE 是否採用雙代幣系統？
否。MAGNE 採用單代幣模式，由 $MHA 支援 Gas、質押、激勵及治理。


任何人都可成為驗證者嗎？
可以。任何人均可成為驗證者，但須同時符合質押要求及節點硬件標準，以確保網絡安全與穩定。


如何選出驗證者？
驗證者並非按固定節點數量決定，而是依據全網質押 $MHA 總量。



活躍驗證者數量將透過治理及社群討論決定。
獎勵分配依據每名驗證者的質押代幣佔全網總質押量比例。
節點較少時，可動態調整獎勵模式，並在需要時採用排名激勵機制。


驗證者的質押要求為何？


每名驗證者最低質押：250,000 $MHA
每名驗證者最高質押：10,000,000 $MHA（可經治理調整）
質押越多，加入活躍驗證者集合及取得較大獎勵份額的機會越高。


驗證者獎勵如何分配？


驗證者獎勵來自 15% 發放池，每年減半。
每名驗證者獎勵份額 =（驗證者質押量 ÷ 全網總質押量）× 年度發放量。
驗證者數量較少時，可透過排名激勵調整分配，以獎勵高品質節點。



節點硬件要求為何？
驗證者須符合最低技術標準，以維持穩定安全運作，包括但不限於：




可靠伺服器基礎設施


高可用性及低網絡延遲


足夠 CPU、RAM、儲存及頻寬


高在線率，以確保出塊及最終確定性
只有符合這些標準的節點，方可獲得驗證者獎勵。




驗證者數量會隨時間改變嗎？
會。驗證者數量是動態的，取決於全網質押量、治理決策及網絡增長。早期驗證者較少時，會調整獎勵分配，以維持公平激勵及網絡安全。


甚麼是排名激勵機制？
當驗證者較少或分配不均時，排名激勵機制確保高效能節點獲得較多獎勵。



驗證者依在線時間、效能及出塊表現排名。
排名越高，獎勵權重越高。
此機制維持網絡穩定，並鼓勵高品質節點營運。



提供流動性後，會自動獲得獎勵嗎？
不會。您須將 LP 代幣質押至相應獎勵金庫，才可獲得 流動性證明（Proof of Liquidity，PoL）獎勵。獎勵會累積，但須手動領取。


如何獲得 PoL 獎勵？



提供流動性並取得 LP 代幣。
將 LP 代幣質押至白名單獎勵金庫。
若驗證者將發放量配置至該金庫，您便會隨時間獲得 $MHA。
從錢包手動領取獎勵。


誰可投票或提交提案？


任何 $MHA 持有人均可參與治理投票。
提交提案可能需要持有最低數量的 $MHA，例如 10,000 枚。
驗證者集合規模、節點要求及發放參數均可透過治理更新。



金庫可將發放量導向特定資金池嗎？
可以。每個獎勵金庫對應特定憑證代幣（例如 LP 代幣）。dApp 可為特定池申請金庫，驗證者則可配置發放量以提升目標流動性。


整體驗證者激勵模式為何？
MAGNE 的驗證者激勵設計基於：




發放量每年減半


按質押權重分配獎勵


動態驗證者集合規模


按排名調整以獎勵優質表現
此模式確保強勁早期激勵、可持續長期獎勵及網絡穩定性。

5.3 術語表
5.3.1 術語表
MagneKit
MagneKit 是 Magne 基於 CometBFT 建立的模組化共識客戶端框架，為行動原生區塊鏈提供相容 EVM 的共識。
Magic Hash（MHA）代幣
$MHA 是 Magne 網絡唯一的原生代幣，用於：

支付交易 Gas 費
質押以運行驗證者
參與治理及流動性證明（Proof of Liquidity，PoL）獎勵
質押 MHA 越多，取得區塊提議權的機會越高

MagneSwap（規劃中）
Magne 的原生去中心化交易所（DEX），支援加權、穩定及可組合流動性池。
PoW（工作量證明）
Magne 的共識機制，由驗證者（礦工）透過運算工作保障網絡安全。出塊權依算力取得；獎勵金庫獎勵等經濟激勵，則由協議層智能合約另行處理。
區塊
包含交易的資料單位，依序加入區塊鏈。
出塊時間
Magne 產生區塊的平均時間，目前約 2 秒。
CometBFT
驅動 MagneKit 的共識引擎，提供高吞吐量及即時最終確定性。
共識客戶端
負責區塊驗證、排序及節點間共識的軟件，通常與執行客戶端配合。
共識機制
Magne 網絡就狀態達成一致的協議。Magne 採用基於質押與參與的流動性證明。
委託
將質押權委派予驗證者，以取得獎勵或治理權的行為。
DEX（去中心化交易所）
讓使用者毋須中介即可兌換代幣的鏈上平台。
Engine API
共識層與執行層之間的通訊介面，支援客戶端模組化。
執行客戶端
處理交易及智能合約的實際執行。Magne 支援基於 Geth 及 Reth 的分支，完全相容以太坊。
最終確定性
已確認交易不能逆轉的保障。Magne 實現單時隙最終確定性。
治理
提出、投票及實施協議變更的流程。治理使用 $MHA 進行。
流動性
可用於交易的代幣數量。流動性越高，兌換越快、滑價越低。
流動性池
持有兩種或以上代幣、用於代幣兌換的智能合約。
流動性提供者
向資金池加入資產，並分享交易費及／或 PoL 獎勵的使用者。
主網
進行真實資產交易的正式網絡，與測試網相對。
單時隙最終確定性
交易在提出的同一區塊內取得最終確認、確保不可逆轉的系統。
質押
鎖定代幣以保障網絡安全或賺取收益的行為，包括驗證者質押及 PoL 收益質押。
兌換
在 DEX 將一種代幣換成另一種代幣的過程，每次兌換均產生費用。
金庫（獎勵金庫）
讓使用者質押 LP 或其他憑證代幣，以獲得基於 PoL 的 $MHA 獎勵的智能合約。

Dapp Hub: Shin Getter Nexus is an upcoming integrated platform designed to serve as the central entry point for decentralized applications within the M Hash ecosystem. It will provide developers and users with seamless access to a wide range of dApps, tools, and services, all connected through a unified interface. With optimized connectivity to both Layer 1 and Layer 2, Shin Getter Nexus aims to enhance cross-application interoperability, reduce friction for onboarding, and foster a thriving decentralized economy.

1.1 What is MAGNE.AI?
MAGNE.AI is a next-generation blockchain platform that merges AI compute infrastructure, DePin networks, and Web3 applications. We aim to build a mobile-native, embedded, and autonomous AI-powered Web3 world.
01 / ECOSYSTEMFrom the device to the networkDEVICEMAGNE.AI PhoneOn-device AI · User interaction↔Applications & developer toolsL1MAGNEBase networkL2M HashApplication executionMHAToken allocation and release rules are documented in Tokenomics.Conceptual reading guide. Relationships and roles shown here describe the whitepaper design, not verified deployment status.
The project is powered by two foundational technologies:

MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain: A mobile-first, EVM-compatible, PoW-based Layer1 chain where smartphones and edge devices can participate in mining and consensus, ensuring security, decentralization, and performance.

MAGNE L1Base network · EVM compatibility

M Hash Layer2 Blockchain: A high-performance Layer 2 network built on opStack with an asynchronous consensus mechanism, separating consensus from execution to significantly boost throughput and efficiency while ensuring security and low-cost transactions.

M Hash L2Application execution · OP Stack design

MAGNE Kit Modular Execution Framework: A re-engineered execution layer optimized for low-latency smart contract processing, tailored for mobile use and AI-native workloads.

MAGNE.AI introduces a novel architecture that fuses AI compute with Web3 infrastructure:

Users earn $MHA tokens by sharing idle compute from devices like the MAGNE.AI Phone Gen1.
Builds a DePin (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure) network where edge devices act as nodes.
Provides AI APIs and SDKs for developers to build decentralized, AI-integrated applications.
Enables on-chain deployment, validation, pricing, and usage of AI models—realizing Web3-native AI-as-a-Service.

The MAGNE.AI ecosystem consists of:

Base infrastructure: MAGNE Layer1, M Hash Layer2
Device matrix: AI-powered phones, earbuds, and glasses (planned)
Application layer: Dapp Hub (Shin Getter Nexus), AI assistants, Web3 games, NFT platforms
Unified token economy: $MHA token used for gas, governance, incentives, staking, and access

MAGNE.AI redefines the boundary between “smart devices” and “decentralized infrastructure,” enabling trusted AI execution, traceable model provenance, data ownership, and multi-device collaboration. Through tight integration of protocol and hardware, MAGNE.AI empowers every user to become a contributor and beneficiary in the AI Web3 era.

1.3 Magic Hash (MHA)
Magic Hash (MHA) is currently issued and transferred as a token on BNB Smart Chain (BSC). The BSC contract disclosed in this whitepaper identifies its current token form.The project plans to migrate and integrate MHA into the MAGNE L1 mainnet and M Hash L2 network as those networks become ready. The migration method, applicable networks, schedule and any actions required of holders will be announced separately.Network stageThe descriptions below of gas, block rewards and halving concern the planned MAGNE network design. They do not describe features already implemented by the current BSC token contract.
MHATOTAL ALLOCATION10,000,000,000 MHATotal allocation, not circulating supply.
Transaction Fees
All on‑chain actions (transfers, contract calls, DApp interactions) pay gas in $MHA. Per protocol design, a portion of the fees is burned (aligned with EVM fee mechanics), reducing circulating supply over time and creating a deflationary pressure that supports long‑term value.
Mining & Security
Blocks are produced via PoW: miners contribute hash power to pack transactions and compete to propose the next block. The successful miner earns block rewards ($MHA) plus transaction fees. Higher aggregate hash rate increases the cost of attacks and strengthens network security.
MAGNE includes optimizations for mobile and edge environments so lightweight nodes/devices can help mine or relay, improving decentralization and network reach.
Issuance & Halving
$MHA issuance follows a planned inflation‑then‑halving schedule: ample rewards in the early phase, then periodic reductions to balance bootstrapping with long‑term scarcity. Block rewards and the fee‑burn mechanism together shape the token’s supply‑and‑sink dynamics.

1.4 What Is Proof-of-Work?
MAGNE Layer 1's PoW Proof-of-Work Mechanism
Proof-of-Work (PoW) is the foundational consensus mechanism of the MAGNE Layer1 network. It relies on computational competition to ensure decentralized trust, secure transaction validation, and network resistance against censorship. Each node must solve cryptographic puzzles to earn block proposal rights, eliminating reliance on trusted intermediaries. At MAGNE.AI, PoW has been reimagined beyond traditional high-energy mining. By integrating with DePin (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure), edge devices like smartphones become mining nodes. This makes consensus participatory and accessible to anyone, aligning network growth with real-world usage. The ultimate vision for MAGNE’s PoW is to create a trustless, mobile-first, and highly secure Layer1 infrastructure for Web3.
Unlike traditional mining that depends on specialized hardware and high energy consumption, MAGNE Layer1 introduces a lightweight form of PoW: mobile mining. Equipped with secure SPU and NPU chips, MAGNE.AI devices allow everyday users to contribute idle computing resources, verify transactions, and earn rewards—ushering in a truly inclusive consensus layer. This is powered by MAGNE’s proprietary DePin infrastructure, where every physical device becomes a node in the blockchain, contributing not just as a user but as a validator of network security. Such participatory design reduces entry barriers to Web3 while enabling more equitable value distribution. By fusing PoW with edge hardware, MAGNE redefines the consensus model for a decentralized future.
In MAGNE Layer1, PoW serves not only as the cornerstone of consensus, but also as a performance accelerator. The project introduces deep architectural enhancements to the EVM by simplifying Merkle Tree structures and integrating intelligent caching. This enables state data to be accessed with minimal disk I/O, improving execution speed. Smart contracts benefit from lower latency and higher throughput, making the network suitable for high-frequency applications. Furthermore, this foundational design aligns with future Layer2 expansion, ensuring smooth data synchronization across modular chains. In MAGNE, PoW is both a shield and an engine—safeguarding the chain while elevating its capabilities.
Inspired by architectures like Berachain’s Proof-of-Liquidity, MAGNE decouples consensus from governance. PoW is strictly focused on securing the network, while decision-making and voting are governed through the MHA token on-chain. This separation of responsibilities allows Layer1 to focus on performance and security, while granting governance power to the broader community—avoiding centralization risks where miners dominate protocol control.

This proposal restores the incentive direction of v1.0 with a separately capped budget. It does not restore its ECU redistribution formula. It is not live: reserve availability, authorization, contracts, quote/acceptance procedures and the effective date must be verified and announced before activation. All rates and the 3,000 MHA staking requirement below remain proposed parameters.
Other participants do not reduce a device’s base reward by choosing an incentive. However, voluntarily locking a portion of your own base reward delays receipt of that portion: the standard 24/36-month claimable totals no longer describe your combined cash-flow schedule. Extra rewards are not included in the standard table or base calculator.

The base curve sums to 400 million before the ramp, and 380 million after its 20 million reduction. This is mathematical budget capacity, not verified free on-chain funds. Reassigning up to 17 million requires confirming that it is uncommitted and authorizing a change of use. No already earned, vested or voluntarily locked user rewards may fund this pool.
The existing annual/monthly emission curve applies to base rewards only. The proposed incentive is a separate spending envelope: maximum base plus incentive awards are 185 million in year 1, 106 million in year 2 and 56 million in year 3, totaling 347 million through M36 before device/work reductions. Lifetime base plus this incentive is capped by 397 million, below the 400 million GEN1 ceiling. This changes the total reward-approval budget and must be disclosed as a substantive revision.
M3–M36 allows no more than 500,000 MHA in newly approved extra rewards per month, and no more than 17,000,000 in total. Unused monthly amounts do not increase later monthly caps. No new awards before M3 or after M36; existing awards and accepted locks continue to maturity, with maturity determined by the actual execution date and chosen term. A 12-month lock executed within M36 can mature in M48; later execution moves maturity later, so M48 is not an unconditional final maturity month. No automatic renewal.
Use one cutoff snapshot per quote batch. B is budget available to this batch after other batches’ valid reservations and approved awards; ΣQ includes only valid, not-yet-reserved requests in this batch, excluding existing quotes. Before executing a lock, recheck that the selected reward is unclaimed and uncommitted; update principal and budget ledgers atomically without duplicate execution. The incentive month means extra-award approval month; record the base earning month separately and assess device-staking eligibility over that earning period. No new approvals after M36; treatment of unaccepted expired quotes and execution deadlines must be published before launch.Voluntary locking: one award per batch
Select all or part of a newly approved monthly base reward, before any of that selected portion is claimed. Locking 6 / 9 / 12 months gives a request ceiling of 10% / 15% / 20% of the selected amount. A 500 MHA selection locked for 12 months requests at most 100 MHA, regardless of the device’s other rewards. The selected portion replaces normal vesting with release in full at maturity. Unselected base rewards keep their original vesting. Existing batches are not retroactively relocked, and the same principal cannot earn a second locking award.
The term runs from the accepted lock execution timestamp. No early withdrawal is modeled. Locking is voluntary and occurs only after the user accepts the final amount, vesting schedule and maturity date. A twelve-month lock receives one incentive for that batch, not twelve monthly interest payments.
Device staking: proposed initial tier
Bind a separate 3,000 MHA deposit to one eligible device. It qualifies from the next settlement month after the deposit is completed, subject to verification, with a monthly request ceiling of 10% of that device’s actual base reward. The same deposit cannot support multiple devices or also serve as voluntarily locked reward principal. Staking without an eligible device or without base rewards creates no reward.
A withdrawal request stops new staking incentive accrual from its timestamp; the final period must be prorated under published settlement rules. Principal is returned after 30 days. No automatic principal slashing is introduced by this proposal. Invalid evidence may affect unapproved rewards under a disclosed review and appeal process. The calculator assumes full-month eligibility and excludes this separate principal’s return.
No stacking; budget-limited quotes
Qᵢ = max(Lᵢ × bᵢ, Eᵢ × sᵢ)k = min(1, B / ΣQᵢ)Xᵢ = Qᵢ × k
E is approved base reward; L is the proposed voluntary-lock amount, capped by E; b is 10%, 15% or 20%; s is 10% for an eligible stake, otherwise zero. Non-selected or ineligible options count as zero. Each device uses one option, taking the higher request without addition or multiplication; ties select staking. B is the smaller of remaining monthly budget (at most 500,000) and remaining authorized program budget (within 17 million). If total requests or available budget are zero, no extra award is made.
Use a published cutoff and deduplicated request snapshot to reserve budgets and issue time-limited quotes. Quotes state the selected option, exact award and principal commitment. Acceptance executes the lock or confirms the staking award. Declined/expired quotes release reservations but do not retrospectively alter accepted awards or trigger automatic repricing. Monthly and lifetime accounting must count both outstanding reservations and accepted awards. No pre-funded lock is required merely to request a locking quote.
Approved extra rewards vest 60% / 20% / 20% from the approval month, independently of voluntary principal maturity. For example, 10,000 devices each earning 1,212.121212… MHA and each requesting a 12-month lock have 242.424242… MHA requests. With 500,000 MHA available and no other requests, each extra award is 50 MHA. This is an earned award, not 50 MHA immediately received.

Calculation basis: reward and vesting formulas
Device-scaled budget
Bₘ = (200,000,000 × 0.5^(y−1) / 12) × rampₘCₘ = min(Bₘ × min(1, Nₘ / 13,750), Nₘ × 10,000)Pₘ = Cₘ / Nₘ
y is the program year. Nₘ counts unique admitted, eligible GEN1 devices for the settlement period, not sales, shipments or wallet addresses. When Nₘ = 0, Cₘ, Pₘ and newly earned rewards are defined as zero without dividing by zero; previously earned batches retain their vesting schedule. Below 13,750 devices, the base mining budget scales down proportionally; at or above it, the budget stops growing and the per-device reference amount falls as participation increases. 13,750 is a budget baseline, not a sales target or device admission cap.
Availability and validated work
Eᵢ,ₘ = Pₘ × (0.20 × Aᵢ,ₘ + 0.80 × Wᵢ,ₘ)
A is the fraction of the entire settlement month during which a device is verified to meet service requirements and be ready to accept tasks. Powering on or connecting to the internet alone does not qualify. W is accepted, quality-adjusted useful work divided by the published full-month GEN1 reference capacity. Both range from 0 to 1, and W ≤ A. Completing every assigned task does not establish W = 1 when demand is low. No accepted tasks means W = 0. An eligible device with A = 1 and W = 0 can earn only the proposed 20% availability component. Invalid, duplicate or self-generated workload is excluded. Unused work rewards are not redistributed to exhaust the pool.
Split a month into non-overlapping subperiods j at eligibility changes. Let dⱼ = Δtⱼ / Tₘ, summing to 1 over the month. Each segment uses only Bₘ × dⱼ of the budget; Nⱼ is its unique eligible device count. A device earns nothing before admission or after departure; Nⱼ = 0 produces no new rewards.Eᵢ,ₘ = Σⱼ [dⱼ × min(Bₘ / max(Nⱼ, 13,750), 10,000) × (0.20 × Aᵢ,ⱼ + 0.80 × Wᵢ,ⱼ)]Aᵢ,ⱼ and Wᵢ,ⱼ use the full segment duration and corresponding reference work capacity, with 0 ≤ Wᵢ,ⱼ ≤ Aᵢ,ⱼ ≤ 1. Do not reuse full-month fractions inside this formula and prorate twice. Reference-capacity conversion, validation/capping of above-reference work and the settlement time zone must be published before launch. The base calculator supports constant counts within each month, not intramonth segments. Track each device and approved batch separately; current counts must not recalculate historical rewards.
Approved, unlocked and actually received
Vesting is indexed to the month in which a reward is earned. After approval, 40% is claimable and the remaining 60% vests in three equal installments, with the first assigned to the same month. The monthly model therefore releases 60%, then 20%, then 20%. Actual approval and claim dates must follow the launch announcement; task completion does not imply an immediate transfer.
Uᵢ,ₘ = 0.60 × Eᵢ,ₘ + 0.20 × Eᵢ,ₘ₋₁ + 0.20 × Eᵢ,ₘ₋₂
Released means scheduled to become claimable after settlement, not a verified transfer to a wallet. Actual receipt depends on completed verification, the published claim process and confirmed transfers. Unactivated devices earn nothing; this proposal applies no blanket 30% pre-activation payment factor or automatic later catch-up. No optional locking or staking reward multiplier is included in the schedule.
Eligibility and verification
Before activation, publish device registration, attestation and deduplication rules, availability sampling, accepted task types, reference benchmark (model, precision and hardware), quality thresholds, review/appeal procedures, claim timing and fees. One physical device must not earn duplicate rewards through multiple accounts. Shared networks alone do not prove abusive ownership. No tasks means no task reward.
Reward rates and applicable limits must be known before tasks are accepted. Reject invalid evidence and review unsettled rewards under published procedures; this draft does not establish a right or technical ability to seize tokens already transferred to a user wallet. Any bonded-stake slashing would require separately disclosed terms and implementation.
Activation and parameter changes
Launch requires disclosed benchmarks, a tested settlement ledger, an executable claim/vesting mechanism, sufficient reserved budget and an effective-date announcement. Review device admission, workload and budget use quarterly. Changes to the baseline, reward split or reference workload require a dated notice, documented authorization and a future effective period; changes must not retroactively rewrite earned batches. Governance and timelocks are not represented as deployed until verified.
Public reporting and methodology
Report eligible device counts, budget ceilings, availability and task rewards, unallocated reserve, earned batches, locked and claimable balances, actual transfers, rule version and exceptions. Budget, earned rewards, claimable rewards and on-chain transfers must remain separate measures.
Budget and vesting inputs originate from the project GEN1 tokenomics model; the 13,750-device baseline was selected for this draft on 1 October 2026. The separation of availability and useful-work rewards draws on Render RNP-021. The 13,750 baseline and 20% / 80% split are MAGNE proposal parameters, not Render parameters or an endorsement. No token price or monetary return is assumed.

1.6 Governance
MAGNE’AI’s governance system enables $MHA holders to directly participate in protocol-level decisions, with voting power proportional to their token holdings. Governance acts as the brain of the network—no changes to core protocol behavior can be enacted without passing through the on-chain governance process, ensuring transparency and decentralized control.
Governance Responsibilities
The governance body is responsible for strategic decision-making regarding protocol operations and long-term direction. Responsibilities include:

Setting fees, staking rewards, and protocol parameters
Approving protocol upgrades and core module replacements
Managing privileged roles and access permissions
Shaping long-term growth, incentives, and ecosystem development

All major changes must go through a formal governance proposal and voting cycle before implementation.
Protocol Roles and Permissions
Manager Role
The Manager is tasked with handling urgent protocol actions requiring immediate execution—such as pausing pools or the vault in case of threats. Managers are also responsible for executing operational changes already approved through governance, allowing fast action within pre-defined governance boundaries.
Authorizer Role
The Authorizer acts as the protocol’s permission controller, connecting governance decisions with executable protocol functions. It ensures secure access control across the system by enforcing authorization logic on every sensitive operation. Working with the governance timelock, it ensures that all changes are vetted and executed securely.
Coordinator Role
The Coordinator oversees the final execution phase of governance proposals. It manages staging, sequencing, and timing of upgrades to ensure all actions follow protocol rules. Coordinators also have emergency powers to cancel or delay changes if issues arise during deployment, maintaining the integrity of the governance process.

1.7 Governance Overview
1.7.1 MAGNE Governance
MAGNE’s decentralized governance system empowers $MHA token holders to steer protocol-level changes including Reward Vault approvals, native dApp configurations, and PoW distribution logic.
Use Cases for Governance:

Whitelisting Reward Vaults (e.g. staking/incentive token approvals)
Configuring native dApps like MAGNESwap (e.g. fee structure)
Adjusting PoL distribution curves or parameters
Upgrading system-level settings or timelock durations


Governance Lifecycle
MAGNE’s governance is based on OpenZeppelin’s battle-tested contracts, providing a secure and transparent multi-phase lifecycle:


Proposal Creation
Any account with sufficient voting power may initiate a proposal


Pending State
Proposals enter a brief 1-hour delay before becoming active for voting


Voting Phase
$MHA holders (or their delegates) can cast votes during the 5-day voting window


Proposal Outcome
If quorum and majority thresholds are met, the proposal is marked as Succeeded


Timelock Queue
Successful proposals enter a 2-day delay queue before execution


Execution
Once timelock elapses, the change can be implemented on-chain by any actor



Guardian Oversight
To protect the protocol from malicious behavior, MAGNE uses a 5-of-9 Guardian Council with the authority to cancel dangerous proposals during the timelock phase (e.g., unauthorized upgrades or asset seizure).

Creating Your Governance Proposal


Ensure You Meet the Voting Threshold
You need at least 10,000 $MHA worth of delegated voting power


Delegate to Yourself
You must explicitly delegate $MHA (even to yourself) to unlock governance rights


Prepare the Proposal Payload
For example, a Reward Vault proposal must include the vault address and correct function call (e.g., addRewardVault(address))


Submit the Proposal
Submit through the on-chain governance contract or via the MAGNEHub UI


Promote the Proposal
Engage the community to build awareness and gather votes


Execute After Timelock
If passed, any user can trigger execution after the 2-day delay



Governance Parameters (Default)
StateCriteriaProposal Creation10,000 $MHA delegated votesPending Period1 hourVoting Period5 daysQuorum Threshold20% of total $MHA supplyTimelock Delay2 days

Reward Vault proposals may follow a simplified governance path. See the Reward Vault Governance Docs for details.

1.8 Incentive Marketplace
In the M Hash Layer2 PoW ecosystem, the Incentive Marketplace allows protocols to offer whitelisted incentive tokens to miners, encouraging them to support specific on-chain activities or liquidity pools. This creates a competitive environment where different protocols vie for miner attention and block reward allocation.
How Incentives Work
When a miner produces a block, they can choose to allocate part of their earned $MHA rewards toward one or more whitelisted Reward Vaults. These vaults are tied to specific protocols or applications.
When rewards are distributed:

The miner receives a commission in incentive tokens from the protocol
The remaining incentive tokens in the vault are distributed to participants who have staked eligible assets in that vault
All claims are processed automatically via M Hash Layer2 Hub
Users can claim their incentives at any time, with no expiration

Roles in the Incentive Marketplace
RoleDescriptionParticipantStakes eligible assets (e.g., LP tokens, NFTs) into a Reward Vault to earn incentivesMinerProduces blocks via PoW and directs part of $MHA rewards to selected vaults in exchange for incentivesProtocolProvides incentive tokens to attract miner-directed rewards and increase engagement/liquidity
Incentive Token Governance

Only whitelisted Reward Vaults may distribute incentive tokens
Each vault can support up to two different incentive tokens
Adding a token or changing its manager requires governance approval

Managing Incentives
The protocol’s Token Manager must set an incentive rate:

Format: “X tokens per MHA”(e.g.,10USDC/MHA” (e.g., 10 USDC/MHA”(e.g.,10USDC/MHA)
The rate cannot be lowered unless the vault’s token balance is fully depleted
Additional tokens can be deposited at any time, and the rate can be increased
Once deposited, incentive tokens cannot be withdrawn

Example:
IncentivesRate$MHA Coverage2000 USDC10/$MHA200 $MHA
Later updated:
New IncentivesNew RateNew Coverage2500 USDC11/$MHA227 $MHA
Commission Distribution

Miners can set a commission rate (default 5%, max 20%) for incentives captured from vaults
Example: If a vault pays 100 USDC for 10 MHA,andaminerwith5MHA, and a miner with 5% commission directs 1 MHA,andaminerwith5MHA worth of rewards, the miner earns 5 USDC, and the remaining 95 USDC goes to vault participants

Timing vs Rate

Distribution timing (e.g., 3-day or 7-day streaming) is set by the Reward Vault
The exchange rate (e.g., 10 USDC/$MHA) remains fixed regardless of the reward release schedule

1.9 Team & Execution
Team & Execution
MAGNE.AI is developed by a multidisciplinary team spanning secure mobile systems, Web3 infrastructure (L1/L2), security engineering, hardware program execution, and global ecosystem operations.
Security & Privacy Engineering
Focused on secure architecture design, certified secure component integration, vulnerability research, and continuous security assurance. This function oversees threat modeling, security reviews across the stack, and incident-response readiness.
Blockchain & Protocol Engineering (L1/L2)
Responsible for protocol development, node infrastructure, performance and stability optimization, and developer tooling that supports ecosystem partners.
Mobile & Wallet Product Engineering
Builds the consumer-facing OS/app layer, wallet and account flows, and user experience abstractions that reduce complexity while preserving self-custody and security.
Hardware Program & Compliance Execution
Leads the end-to-end device program including platform selection, supplier integration, validation and ramp phases (EVT/DVT/PVT), and certification readiness across regions.
Business Development & Ecosystem Operations
Drives partner onboarding, exchange and institutional coordination, and compliance-aware operations—supporting partner due diligence and compliance processes (e.g., KYC/AML-related workflows where applicable)—alongside global community growth.
Extended Contributors & Partners
In addition to the core team, MAGNE.AI is supported by extended contributors and strategic partners across manufacturing, component supply, certification services, and ecosystem development to accelerate delivery and ensure production-grade quality.
Governance & Delivery Discipline
MAGNE.AI maintains clear separation of responsibilities across product, engineering, security, and operations, supported by standardized development processes and controlled release management. Public communications follow a disclosure policy designed to ensure accuracy and avoid forward-looking listing or price-related statements. Detailed team and certification materials are available for exchanges, partners, and regulators through controlled due diligence processes.
Note: For privacy and security reasons, certain biographies and credentials may be presented in summarized form. Detailed information is available under NDA / controlled review.

1.10 MAGNE Layer2 Metrics
Compared with other Layer 2 scaling solutions on PoW-based or Ethereum-compatible Layer 1 chains, M Hash Layer2 delivers lower gas fees and a higher block gas limit, ensuring that gas fees remain stable even as Layer 2 traffic increases. The table below references standard EIP-1559 parameters for comparison, noting that some L2s (e.g., Arbitrum) use custom gas mechanisms like ArbOS, which are not directly comparable.

While the OP Stack has minor differences between implementations, M Hash Layer2 applies its own set of optimizations — including PoW-tailored caching improvements, parallel execution scheduling, and optimized batching for transaction inclusion — to push throughput to 100M gas per second, far surpassing the base MAGNE Layer 1 chain.
1.10.3 M Hash Layer2 vs MAGNE Layer1 vs Ethereum Layer1

4.3 Build A Smart Contract
4.3.1 MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain
4.3.2 Deploy Smart Contracts

A guide to help you get started with deploying your smart contracts on MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain.

Welcome to the MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain deployment quickstart guide! This comprehensive walkthrough will help you set up your environment and deploy smart contracts on MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain. Whether you're a seasoned developer or just starting out, this guide has got you covered.
4.3.3 What You'll Achieve
By the end of this quickstart, you'll be able to:

Set up your development environment to deploy on MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain
Deploy your smart contracts to MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain
Connect your frontend to your smart contracts
Why MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain?

MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain is a mobile-first, EVM-compatible, PoW-based Layer1 chain where smartphones and edge devices can participate in mining and consensus, ensuring security, decentralization, and performance.
4.3.4 Set Up Your Development Environment

Create a new project directory

Copymkdir my-MAGNE-project && cd my-MAGNE-project


Install Foundry, a powerful framework for smart contract development

Copycurl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup

This installs Foundry and updates it to the latest version.

Initialize a new Solidity project

Copy
Copyforge init

Your Foundry project is now ready. You'll find an example contract in the src directory, which you can replace with your own contracts. For the purposes of this guide, we'll use the Counter contract provided in src/Counter.sol
Foundry provides a suite of tools for EVM application development, including Forge (for testing), Cast (for interacting with the chain), and Anvil (for setting up a local node). You can learn more about Foundry here.
4.3.5 Configure Foundry with MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain
To deploy your smart contracts to MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain, you need two key components:

A node connection to interact with the MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain network
A funded private key to deploy the contract

Let's set up both of these:
1. Set up your node connection

Create a .env file in your project's root directory
Add the MagicalHash network RPC URL to your .env file

CopyMAGICAL_RPC_URL="https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com"


Load your environment variables

Copysource .env

Magne L1 Testnet is the test network for MAGNE Layer1 Blockchain, which we will use for the rest of this guide. You can obtain free MHA from one of the faucets .
2. Secure your private key

Store your private key in Foundry's secure keystore

Copycast wallet import deployer --interactive


When prompted enter your private key and a password.

Your private key is stored in ~/.foundry/keystores which is not tracked by git.
Never share or commit your private key. Always keep it secure and handle with care.
4.3.6 Deploy Your Contracts
Now that your environment is set up, let's deploy your contracts to Magne L1 Testnet.

Use the following command to compile and deploy your contract

Copyforge create ./src/Counter.sol:Counter --rpc-url $MAGICAL_RPC_URL --account deployer

Note the format of the contract being deployed is <contract-path>:<contract-name>.

After successful deployment, the transaction hash will be printed to the console output
Copy the deployed contract address and add it to your .env file

CopyCOUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS="0x..."


Load the new environment variable

Copysource .env

Verify Your Deployment
To ensure your contract was deployed successfully:

Check the transaction on https://explorer.testnet.magicalhash.com.
Use the cast command to interact with your deployed contract from the command line

Copycast call $COUNTER_CONTRACT_ADDRESS "number()(uint256)" --rpc-url $MAGNE_RPC_URL

This will return the initial value of the Counter contract's number storage variable, which will be 0.
Congratulations! You've deployed your smart contracts to MAGNE L1 chain!

4.4 Launch an ERC-20 Token with Foundry

4.4.1 Requirements


Foundry v1.3.1+
Copycurl -L https://foundry.paradigm.xyz | bash
foundryup

(Foundry v1.3.1+ is required for Etherscan V2 verification.)



4.4.2 Create the project
Copymkdir launch-mha-token && cd launch-mha-token
forge init

This creates the standard Foundry project scaffold.

4.4.3 Install OpenZeppelin + set remappings
Copyforge install OpenZeppelin/openzeppelin-contracts
echo 'remappings = ["@openzeppelin/contracts/=lib/openzeppelin-contracts/contracts/"]' >> foundry.toml


This ensures your IDE resolves OpenZeppelin imports correctly.

4.4.4 Write the ERC-20 contract
Rename the default file:
Copymv src/Counter.sol src/MagnetToken.sol

src/MagnetToken.sol:
Copy// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import {ERC20} from "@openzeppelin/contracts/token/ERC20/ERC20.sol";

contract MagnetToken is ERC20 {
    constructor(
        string memory name_,
        string memory symbol_,
        uint256 initialSupply
    ) ERC20(name_, symbol_) {
        _mint(msg.sender, initialSupply);
    }
}

Compile to confirm:
Copyforge compile


4.4.5 Create a deploy script
Rename the sample script and update it:
Copymv script/Counter.s.sol script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol

script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol:
Copy// SPDX-License-Identifier: UNLICENSED
pragma solidity ^0.8.20;

import {Script, console2} from "forge-std/Script.sol";
import {MagnetToken} from "../src/MagnetToken.sol";

contract DeployMagnetToken is Script {
    function run() public {
        vm.startBroadcast();
        // Example: 1,000,000 tokens (18 decimals)
        MagnetToken token = new MagnetToken("Magic Hash", "MHA", 1_000_000 ether);
        vm.stopBroadcast();

        console2.log("address:", address(token));
        console2.log("totalSupply:", token.totalSupply());
    }
}



4.4.6 (Optional) Adjust tests
Copymv test/Counter.t.sol test/MagnetToken.t.sol

You can keep it empty or add your own token tests.

4.4.7 Create a Foundry keystore wallet
Copycast wallet import MyMagneAccount --interactive
# paste private key, set password

This account will be used for deployment.

4.4.8 Local dry-run (optional)
Copyanvil
# new terminal:
forge script script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol \
  --account MyMagneAccount \
  --fork-url https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com \
  --broadcast


You’ll see the deployed address and total supply logs.

4.4.9 Deploy to MAGNE L1 Testnet
Make sure the wallet has MAGNE L1 testnet tokens for gas.
Copyforge script script/DeployMagnetToken.s.sol \
  --account MyMagneAccount \
  --rpc-url https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com \
  --broadcast


The output will include the transaction hash and your deployed contract address.

💡 You can adapt this for mainnet by switching to your mainnet RPC (e.g. https://rpc.magicalhash.com).


4.4.10 Verify the contract on MAGNE L1  explorer
MAGNE.AI uses Etherscan-compatible verification. You’ll need an API key:
Copyforge verify-contract \
  --watch \
  --chain magne-ai-testnet \
  <0xYOUR_DEPLOYED_CONTRACT_ADDRESS> \
  src/MagnetToken.sol:MagnetToken \
  --verifier etherscan \
  --etherscan-api-key <YOUR_API_KEY>


Once verified, the contract page will be visible on MAGNE L1 explorer.

4.4.11 Quick Checklist

✅ Token name / symbol ("Magic Hash", "MHA")
✅ Initial supply with ether (18 decimals)
✅ RPC: https://rpc.testnet.magicalhash.com/
✅ Wallet: MyMagneAccount
✅ API key for verification
✅ Testnet MAGNE balance for gas

3.2 Why M Hash Layer2 is Built on OP Stack
Before building M Hash Layer2, our team conducted extensive research and evaluation of available Layer 2 frameworks. We ultimately chose the OP Stack as the foundation for M Hash Layer2 Rollup because of its modularity, high performance potential, and alignment with our goals.
3.2.1 Our Goals

Achieve up to 100M gas per second throughput. We optimized EVM execution, state storage, and transaction handling to push the upper limits of Layer 2 performance.
Deliver an extremely low-cost rollup solution. Since Layer 1 calldata costs dominate rollup fees, we designed M Hash Layer2 to support flexible Data Availability (DA) layers beyond mainnet posting—significantly reducing gas overhead.
Contribute to open infrastructure. All performance optimizations and research from M Hash Layer2 will be open-sourced and shared with the broader OP Stack ecosystem.

3.2.2 Why OP Stack

Modular Execution Clients: OP Stack allows M Hash Layer2 to plug in different execution clients for performance tuning or decentralization. We can integrate with existing BSC-compatible clients or build our own execution layer.
Flexible Data Availability: OP Stack separates execution and DA layers. M Hash Layer2 can choose between Ethereum DA, BNB Greenfield, or future custom DA layers to balance security, scalability, and cost.
Ecosystem Interoperability: As part of the OP Stack ecosystem, M Hash Layer2 can connect with other rollups like Optimism. This enhances network effects, increases composability, and fosters collaboration between ecosystems.

3.3 Why MAGNE.AI Needs Layer2
Layer 1 (L1) is the base settlement and security layer responsible for data propagation and consensus — in our ecosystem, this is MAGNE (PoW, native token $MHA). When popular applications (GameFi, SocialFi, memecoin launches, NFT minting, etc.) bring in massive interaction volumes within a short period, L1 can easily become congested during peak times: gas fees spike, confirmations slow down, user experience degrades, and other dApps on the same chain may also be affected.
To address this, L1 needs scalability — the ability to process more transactions per second without compromising security. In practice, purely scaling a single chain often sacrifices decentralization or security boundaries. A more viable path is to introduce Layer 2 (L2) — in our case, M Hash Layer2 (built on opStack, leveraging asynchronous batch consensus, low cost, and high throughput).
3.3.1 Challenges for L1 During Peak Loads

Transaction Congestion: When daily transactions surge to the millions, L1 block space becomes scarce, with noticeable queuing and packing delays.
Fee Spikes: Gas bidding drives up interaction costs, pricing out new users and long-tail use cases, stalling application growth.
Spillover Performance Impact: Traffic spikes from a single high-volume dApp can slow confirmation times and finality for all other applications on the chain.


Example: If a Web3 game generates 8,000,000+ transactions/day during peak periods, processing solely on L1 would not only cause confirmation delays and synchronization strain but could also push daily gas costs to unsustainable levels, suppressing genuine user growth and retention.

3.3.2 How M Hash Layer2 (L2) Helps

Offloads Computation & Data: Executes and aggregates batches of transactions on L2 before posting summaries to L1; L1 focuses on security and final settlement, while L2 handles high-frequency, low-cost execution.
High Throughput, Low Fees: With opStack’s execution/consensus separation and asynchronous batching, throughput increases significantly, while the marginal cost per transaction drops — ideal for high-frequency use cases (trading, gaming, social, payments).
Composable & Compatible: EVM-compatible, allowing developers and users to use familiar toolchains and wallets; seamless bridging of assets and state between L1 and L2.
Security Preserved: Data and finality are anchored to L1 (MAGNE/PoW/$MHA), ensuring decentralization and security boundaries remain intact while scaling.

3.3.3 Positive Impact on $MHA and the Ecosystem

Fee Relief: Migrating most high-frequency interactions to L2 reduces gas pressure on L1 $MHA, preventing block space bidding wars during peak times.
Stronger Network Effects: Lower costs and higher performance attract more real users and developers, in turn increasing L1 settlement and security demand (hash power and economic security grow).
Sustainable Growth: Popular dApps can scale without “crowding out” the entire chain’s experience, enabling parallel ecosystem expansion and avoiding the “growth = congestion” trap.

Conclusion:
MAGNE (L1/PoW/$MHA) provides security and finality, while M Hash Layer2 (L2) delivers high throughput and low fees. Together, they ensure that even under extreme application loads, the ecosystem remains usable, affordable, and sustainable — without sacrificing decentralization or security.

3.5 High-Security Applications
High-Security Applications
MAGNE Layer1 ensures robust security through Proof-of-Work consensus and on-chain transparent auditing.
All transactions, contract executions, and fund flows are publicly verifiable and immutable on the blockchain.
This makes it ideal for applications requiring the highest security standards, such as financial services, decentralized governance, supply chain data verification, and compliance audits.
Users and institutions can independently verify system integrity without relying on third parties, reducing trust costs and strengthening overall credibility.

3.6 M Hash Layer2 Optimizations on OP Stack
To maximize throughput and reduce gas fees on M Hash Layer2 Rollup, we introduced multiple performance optimizations across the Execution and Derivation layers of the OP Stack. These enhancements build upon research and engineering efforts tailored to high-throughput Layer 2 networks.
Execution Layer Optimizations
EVM State Access Optimization
In M Hash Layer2, we optimized how the EVM accesses state by improving cache hierarchy. Similar to BSC’s "SharedPool" concept, we introduced a Level 1.5 (L1.5) cache to improve data access efficiency between in-memory and dik-level storage, reducing latency in execution.
Improved Bloom Filter Accuracy in Diff Layer
Bloom filters are used to check the presence of key-value pairs during state lookups. However, large datasets increase false positives. M Hash Layer2 reduces the Diff Layer depth from 128 to 32, shrinking the filter’s data footprint and cutting down on unnecessary recursive cache lookups. This significantly improves EVM state retrieval efficiency.
Efficient Prefetching with Shared Cache
Prefetching accelerates transaction processing by preloading state data into cache before block execution. Previously, separate caches between the main and prefetch threads limited performance. We now use a shared world state pool (originStorage), allowing both threads to access L1.5 cache directly. This design dramatically improves cache hit rates during block processing.
L2 Block Production Caching
During block proposal, transactions are often executed twice: once during production and again upon payload commit. We resolved this by introducing a caching layer that stores execution results from the initial run. Upon receiving the finalization call (engine_newPayloadV1), M Hash Layer2 retrieves the precomputed payload directly from cache, reducing latency.
Derivation Layer Optimizations
Asynchronous Batch Submission
Previously, the batcher would wait for 15 confirmations (~45s) on L1 before submitting a new batch. To increase throughput, we implemented asynchronous submission. Now, batches are sent without waiting, while a background watcher monitors for L1 reorgs. If reorgs occur, affected batches are re-submitted. This upgrade greatly improves L2 throughput and is scheduled for future mainnet release.

2.1 Gas and Fees
M Hash Layer2 is a chain scaling solution built on top of the MAGNE Layer 1 blockchain, designed to deliver high throughput and low-cost transactions for DeFi, NFTs, gaming, and other high-demand applications.
The cost of an M Hash Layer2  transaction consists of two components:

Layer 2 gas fee – reflects the computational complexity of processing the transaction on M Hash L2
Layer 1 gas fee – covers the cost of submitting batched transactions to the MAGNE mainnet for verification and finality

Gas price formula:
Gas price = base price + priority price
Transaction cost formula:
L2 transaction cost = (L2 gas price × L2 gas consumed) + (L1 gas price × L1 gas consumed)

Current Configuration
NetworkFloor Base PriceMinimum Priority PriceM Hash L2 Testnet0 gwei1 gweiM Hash L2 MainnetMAGNE L1 Testnet0 gwei0.1 gweiMAGNE L1 Mainnet

What This Means
The floor base price is the minimum base gas price that M Hash can set. This value can change dynamically depending on network usage.
For example, with the current configuration, if a block’s usage reaches 50% of the 100M gas limit, the base price will rise by 12.5%.
The minimum priority price is preset. Users can choose any priority fee higher than this minimum.
Typically, wallets and dApps retrieve the recommended gas price by calling the “estimate gas price” API, which calculates it based on the average gas price from recent blocks.
M Hash’s goal is to keep basic transfer transactions under $0.001, enabling mass adoption and supporting high-frequency, low-value use cases.
How M Hash Layer2 Keeps Costs Low

Enhanced Data Compression – Apply advanced compression algorithms to minimize L2 transaction data before submitting to L1
Efficient Transaction Batching – Optimize batching to maximize block space usage and reduce per-transaction costs
Data Availability Solutions – Leverage MAGNE’s data availability infrastructure to offload some storage from L1, lowering costs
Zero-Knowledge Proofs – Validate transactions without exposing full transaction data, reducing L1 data load
Protocol-Level Optimizations – Improve protocol execution and networking to lower computational overhead on L2

3.8 POAi and DePIN Integration: The Edge Revolution of MAGNE.AI
MAGNE.AI Phone Gen1 is more than just a smartphone—it is a node in the global distributed AI and blockchain network. By integrating POAi (Proof of AI) with DePIN (Decentralized Physical Infrastructure Networks), MAGNE.AI transforms every device into both a blockchain validator and an AI computing contributor.
1. AI Computation Contribution (POAi)

Users can contribute idle device computing power to perform AI tasks, such as inference, model training, or data analytics
Contributions are transparent, verifiable, and recorded on-chain
Every computation generates a Proof of AI, which rewards users with $MHA tokens

2. Participation in DePIN Networks

Every MAGNE.AI device becomes an edge node in the DePIN ecosystem, supporting decentralized storage, bandwidth sharing, and IoT connectivity

AI training and inference can be executed across millions of devices in parallel

2.3.1 Layer2 Architecture
The Layer2 architecture of MAGNE.AI - M Hash Layer2  is designed to meet the high concurrency, low latency, and real-time interaction needs of modern Web3 applications. Built on an optimized version of the opStack framework, it discards traditional consensus mechanisms in favor of a streamlined structure that emphasizes speed and responsiveness. The system consists only of two key roles: the execution node (opgas) and the state synchronizer (opnode), enabling greater efficiency while maintaining data integrity.
The opgas node executes block transactions in batches without requiring confirmation of each individual operation. Once a batch is complete, the opnode verifies the entire set in one consensus step. This asynchronous batch processing design breaks the traditional synchronous execution bottleneck, making it ideal for high-performance applications such as trading platforms, blockchain games, social apps, and payment solutions.
Each on-chain application is implemented as a Rollup with its own execution logic, providing flexibility and isolation. Through a unified, high-performance API layer, developers can seamlessly interact with both on-chain and off-chain data. The architecture is mobile-friendly by design, enabling users to access Web3 features directly through dedicated apps without relying on browsers or extensions.
Despite eliminating consensus protocols, M Hash Layer2  maintains strong consistency and security. It achieves this with multi-layer validation, replay protection, and fault recovery features. Combined with the modular design of opStack, M Hash Layer2  is highly customizable and scalable to support the evolving needs of Web3 ecosystems.
In summary, M Hash Layer2  represents a new paradigm in high-performance blockchain infrastructure. With simplified consensus, parallelized processing, and an intuitive user experience, it provides the technical foundation for the next generation of Web3 innovation and lightweight chain architecture.
2.3.2 Layer2 Innovation
MAGNE.AI introduces a novel Asynchronous Consensus Mechanism within its M Hash Layer2  design by decoupling transaction execution (opgas) from consensus operations (opnode). This architecture significantly improves scalability, throughput, and responsiveness for high-performance Web3 and AI-integrated applications.
In traditional Layer2 Rollup systems, execution and ordering are tightly coupled, meaning all transactions must be processed sequentially by the same validator or sequencer set. While simple, this design limits parallelism and creates bottlenecks under high transaction volumes or complex workloads like on-chain AI inference.
M Hash Layer2  separates these concerns via two core components:

opgas (Execution Layer): Handles transaction logic, contract execution, and AI model inference independently.
opnode (Consensus Layer): Responsible for batching, ordering, and submitting verified results to Layer1.

By running these layers asynchronously, multiple opgas units can process transactions in parallel—pre-executing and caching results—while opnode finalizes consensus and posting to the base chain. This structure minimizes synchronization delays and maximizes execution efficiency.
Key benefits of this architecture include:

Higher Throughput: Multiple execution lanes can handle concurrent transactions and compute-heavy operations.
Lower Latency: Users experience faster interaction via local pre-confirmation and execution buffering.
Modular Scalability: opgas and opnode layers can be independently scaled and deployed across distributed networks.
Resilient Validation: Asynchronous design enables flexible result merging and conflict resolution before final commitment.

This makes M Hash Layer2  particularly suited for AI x Web3 scenarios, where smart contracts, real-time inference, and data availability must coexist at scale. The asynchronous consensus model empowers true parallelism, paving the way for the next generation of responsive, intelligent decentralized applications.
